question: In acute gouty arthritis, monosodium urate (MSU) crystals deposited in the joint activate which specific intracellular pathway in synovial macrophages to drive the inflammatory attack?

answers.text: The NLRP3 inflammasome, triggering caspase-1 activation and massive IL-1β release

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. MSU crystals are phagocytosed by synovial macrophages and activate the NLRP3 inflammasome. This triggers caspase-1 and massive IL-1β release, driving neutrophil recruitment and the intense inflammatory response of acute gout. This mechanism explains why colchicine (disrupts microtubule-dependent inflammasome assembly) and IL-1 inhibitors (anakinra) are effective.

answers.text: The COX-2 pathway, directly generating prostaglandins from crystal surfaces

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: MSU crystals do not directly generate prostaglandins. While COX-derived prostaglandins contribute downstream, the initiating event is NLRP3 inflammasome activation leading to IL-1β release. NSAIDs help by blocking COX-mediated amplification, but the primary crystal-sensing mechanism is the inflammasome.

answers.text: The classical complement cascade via C1q binding to crystal surfaces

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While complement activation can contribute to crystal-induced inflammation, the dominant intracellular pathway through which macrophages sense MSU crystals is the NLRP3 inflammasome → IL-1β axis. This is the specific mechanism targeted by colchicine and IL-1 inhibitors.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While TLR signalling may play a secondary role, the primary intracellular sensor for MSU crystals is the NLRP3 inflammasome. The resulting IL-1β release is the central driver of acute gout, mechanistically distinct from TLR4-mediated bacterial recognition.

overallFeedback.feedback: MSU crystals activate the NLRP3 inflammasome in synovial macrophages, triggering caspase-1 and massive IL-1β release. This drives neutrophil recruitment and the intense acute inflammatory response — the mechanism targeted by colchicine and IL-1 inhibitors.

Well recalled. The NLRP3 inflammasome → IL-1β axis is the critical molecular driver of acute gout, explaining why colchicine (inhibits microtubule-dependent inflammasome assembly) and anakinra (IL-1 receptor antagonist) are effective treatments.
